market_mood: Two forces dominate: Middle East escalation (Hormuz mines, Egypt possibly joining the Saudi-Houthi fight) keeping oil near five-month highs, and a credit-driven wobble in the AI infrastructure trade as investors question debt-funded data center buildouts. M&A stayed heavy, with deals in packaging, optics, nuclear fuel and biotech.
self_check: My merger-and-deal calls have been the best bucket (68%) while high-confidence picks have badly underperformed (2 of 8), so today I leaned into concrete M&A catalysts and kept position sizing of conviction more modest.

picks.reason: Silgan is buying Trivium in a $3.4B deal that meaningfully expands its metal packaging footprint; acquirers in steady cash-flow packaging often grind higher as accretion math sinks in over weeks.
TTM is buying MKS's Ophir Optics unit for $650M, adding high-margin defense and thermal-imaging optics at a time defense demand is soaring.
Centrus is buying centrifuge supplier Westerman for $116M, vertically integrating its enrichment buildout just as nuclear fuel security stays a policy priority.
H.B. Fuller rejected Ancora's revised $1.4B bid for its adhesives business, which keeps activist pressure and the prospect of a higher offer or breakup alive.
Credit default swap costs on Oracle are rising as investors question debt-funded AI buildouts; that overhang tends to grind on for weeks rather than resolve in a day.
Apple's foldable iPhone Duo selling out in minutes points to a new upgrade cycle that benefits suppliers and contract manufacturers the market hasn't fully re-rated.

watchlist_notes.note: Index bounced Monday but is down on the week as oil-driven inflation worries and AI credit stress fight a strong staples/energy rotation.
Tech was the worst sector last week (-5%) on AI debt concerns; Oracle credit spreads are the thing to watch.
Dow holding up better than Nasdaq thanks to defensives and defense/industrial earnings this week.
At record highs on sold-out iPhone Duo foldable preorders, though some analysts flag slowing iPhone 18 demand.
Copilot Studio autonomous agents preview keeps the AI monetization story alive, but no major new headline today.
Rebounded Monday and won CPU business from AI cloud Modal, a small share grab from Intel and AMD.
Morgan Stanley named it top pick with a $350 target on AWS strength, though free cash flow is negative on capex.
No major news today beyond partner-level AI announcements.
Morgan Stanley raised its target, but a strategist flagged off-balance-sheet lease financing ballooning toward $600B ahead of earnings this week.
Chatter about a SpaceX merger and Musk's SpaceX share giveaway pledge are headline noise, not confirmed deals.
Expanding JPM Coin to Ethereum, a modest positive for its blockchain payments franchise.
Oil near five-month highs after Hormuz tanker mine strikes supports earnings, though prices eased on sanctions-waiver news.
Gold stays supported by Middle East escalation, French unrest and European debt jitters.
Oil-driven food and energy inflation plus European bond stress argue against a rally in long bonds.

top_buys.pitch: A cheap, well-timed $650M optics acquisition that pushes TTM further into high-margin defense.
top_buys.why: TTM is buying MKS's Ophir Optics business, adding infrared optics used in targeting, thermal imaging and missile seekers. Defense budgets are expanding globally, with RTX and GE Aerospace reporting into soaring demand this week. Deals like this tend to be re-rated gradually as analysts update models, not all on day one.
top_buys.risks: Integration costs and a dilutive financing structure could pressure near-term margins, and TTM also has cyclical commercial PCB exposure that is tied to the wobbling AI capex trade.
top_buys.watch: TTM's upcoming quarterly results and any detail on how the Ophir deal is funded.

top_buys.pitch: A $3.4B bolt-on makes Silgan a bigger player in defensive metal packaging just as staples lead the market.
top_buys.why: Silgan and American Industrial Partners are buying Trivium, a large metal packaging business, in a deal valued at $3.4B. Consumer staples was the strongest sector last week (+3.3%), and food inflation headlines point to steady can and container volumes. Packaging acquirers with recurring cash flow typically see estimate upgrades over several weeks.
top_buys.risks: The deal adds leverage at a time when credit markets are nervous, and aluminum/steel input costs could squeeze margins.
top_buys.watch: Silgan's next earnings call for accretion guidance and financing terms on the Trivium deal.

top_buys.pitch: Oracle has become the market's chosen stress test for debt-funded AI buildouts.
top_buys.why: Investors are paying up for protection against an Oracle default, and the broader AI picks-and-shovels trade reversed hard last week as borrowing costs for GPU buildouts drew scrutiny. CoreWeave fell 20% in a week and Nebius 25%, showing the market is actively repricing AI leverage. Credit worries usually unwind over weeks, not a single session.
top_buys.risks: A strong Meta or hyperscaler result this week could reignite AI enthusiasm and squeeze shorts hard; Oracle's backlog remains enormous.
top_buys.watch: Oracle CDS spreads and Meta's earnings report this week.

top_buys.pitch: Buying its own centrifuge supplier removes a bottleneck in the US enrichment buildout.
top_buys.why: Centrus agreed to acquire Westerman for $116M, securing a key supplier for the centrifuges it needs to scale domestic uranium enrichment. With Russia sanctions policy in flux and energy security in focus, domestic enrichment capacity has strong policy tailwinds. Vertical integration de-risks a program whose main criticism has been execution speed.
top_buys.risks: LEU is highly volatile and richly valued; any Russia sanctions relief that reopens cheap enrichment supply would undercut the thesis.
top_buys.watch: Any US government funding announcement on HALEU and Trump's 60-day decision on Russia sanctions.

top_buys.pitch: Rejecting a raised $1.4B activist bid rarely ends the story.
top_buys.why: H.B. Fuller turned down Ancora's revised offer for its adhesives business, which signals management thinks the unit is worth more and keeps the activist pressure on. Situations like this often lead to a higher bid, a strategic review or a broader breakup that surfaces value. Materials was one of the strongest sectors last week, which helps the setup.
top_buys.risks: Ancora could simply walk away, leaving the stock to trade on soft industrial adhesive demand and no catalyst.
top_buys.watch: Any Ancora response letter or H.B. Fuller announcement of a formal strategic review.
